simple.meaning: תְּקוּפָה (tᵉqûwphâh) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “a revolution , i.e. (of the sun) course , (of time) lapse.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 4 times across Exodus, 1 Samuel, 2 Chronicles, Psalms, beginning at Exodus 34:22. Its contexts include family line, Torah, kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to תְּקוּפָה (H8622).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: תְּקוּפָה (tᵉqûwphâh) / H8622 is traced through Exodus 34:22, 1 Samuel 1:20, 2 Chronicles 24:23, Psalms 19:7 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.short: a revolution , i.e. (of the sun) course , (of time) lapse
definitions.full: H8622. tequphah [ תְּקוּפָה ] noun feminine coming round, circuit ; — construct הַשָּׁנָה תְּקוּפַת Exod 34:22 (JE), adverb, at the circuit (completion) of the year , so ׳לִת הַשָּׁנָה 2Chron 24:33; = plural construct הַיָּמִים לִתְקֻפוֺת 1Sam 1:20 ; singular suffix of finished circuit of sun Psa 19:7 (opposed to מוֺצָאוֺ ; compare of moon, בתקופתו Ecclus 43:7).

occurrences.englishText: “You shall observe the feast of weeks with the first fruits of wheat harvest, and the feast of harvest at the year’s end.
When the time had come, Hannah conceived, and bore a son; and she named him Samuel,‡ Samuel sounds like the Hebrew for “heard by God.” saying, “Because I have asked him of Yahweh.”

At the end of the year, the army of the Syrians came up against him: and they came to Judah and Jerusalem, and destroyed all the princes of the people from among the people, and sent all their plunder to the king of Damascus.
Yahweh’s law is perfect, restoring the soul.
